subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In which type of collision is kinetic energy conserved?
questions.explain: Kinetic energy is conserved only in perfectly elastic collisions; momentum is conserved in all of them.

questions.q: Two points on a wave are separated by a path difference of one full wavelength. What is their phase difference?
questions.explain: One whole wavelength corresponds to a phase difference of 360° (2π radians).

questions.q: On a velocity–time graph, the gradient represents:
questions.explain: The gradient of a velocity–time graph is the acceleration.

questions.q: For a projectile launched on level ground, which launch angle gives the maximum range (no air resistance)?
questions.explain: Maximum horizontal range occurs at a launch angle of 45° on level ground.

questions.q: Total internal reflection can occur only when light travels:
options: From a more dense to a less dense medium at an angle above the critical angle
From a less dense to a more dense medium
questions.explain: TIR requires light passing from a higher to a lower refractive index medium at an angle exceeding the critical angle.

questions.q: On a displacement–time graph, the gradient at a point represents:
questions.explain: The gradient of a displacement–time graph is the instantaneous velocity.

questions.q: Light travels from air into glass of refractive index 1.5. Using Snell's law, if the angle of incidence is 30°, the angle of refraction is approximately:
questions.explain: n₁sinθ₁ = n₂sinθ₂: sinθ₂ = (1×sin30)/1.5 = 0.333, θ₂ ≈ 19.5°.

questions.q: A pipe open at both ends has length 0.85 m. Taking speed of sound as 340 m/s, what is its fundamental frequency?
questions.explain: For an open pipe λ = 2L = 1.7 m, so f = v/λ = 340/1.7 = 200 Hz.

questions.q: A wave has frequency 50 Hz and travels at 340 m/s. What is its wavelength?
questions.explain: Using v = fλ, λ = 340/50 = 6.8 m.

questions.q: A 0.15 kg cricket ball is struck and its velocity changes by 30 m s⁻¹ over 0.010 s. The average force on the ball is:
The principle of superposition states that when two waves meet, the resultant displacement is:
options: The vector sum of the individual displacements
The larger of the two displacements
The product of the individual displacements
questions.explain: Superposition states the resultant displacement equals the (vector) sum of the individual displacements.

questions.q: In a step-index optical fibre, the cladding has a lower refractive index than the core in order to:
options: Allow total internal reflection to keep light in the core
Increase the speed of light in the core
questions.explain: A lower-index cladding ensures total internal reflection at the core-cladding boundary, confining the light.

questions.q: For two coherent waves to interfere destructively, the path difference must be:
options: A whole number of wavelengths, nλ
An odd number of half wavelengths, (n + ½)λ
questions.explain: Destructive interference occurs when the path difference is an odd number of half-wavelengths, (n+½)λ.

questions.q: A motor lifts a 50 kg load at constant speed through 10 m in 20 s. The useful power output is: (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
Using a diffraction grating with d = 1.5 × 10⁻⁶ m and light of wavelength 500 nm, what is the highest order maximum that can be observed?
questions.explain: Maximum n when sinθ ≤ 1: n ≤ d/λ = 1.5×10⁻⁶/500×10⁻⁹ = 3, so n = 3.

questions.q: Light travels from a medium of refractive index 1.5 toward air. The critical angle for total internal reflection is approximately:
Monochromatic light of wavelength 600 nm strikes a grating with d = 2.0 × 10⁻⁶ m. At what angle does the first-order maximum appear?
Which property is unique to transverse waves and cannot occur with longitudinal waves?
questions.explain: Polarisation requires oscillations perpendicular to propagation, so only transverse waves can be polarised.

questions.q: A car travels at constant velocity along a straight road. What can be said about the forces on it?
options: The driving force equals the total resistive force
There is a net forward force
questions.explain: Constant velocity means zero resultant force, so the driving force balances the resistive forces.

questions.q: Compared with a double slit, a diffraction grating produces maxima that are:
options: Sharper, brighter and more widely separated
questions.explain: The many slits of a grating give sharper, brighter, and more widely spaced maxima.

questions.q: A stationary wave is formed on a string fixed at both ends. The distance between adjacent nodes is:
questions.explain: Adjacent nodes (or antinodes) on a stationary wave are separated by half a wavelength.

questions.q: Two loudspeakers emit sound in phase. At a point where the path difference is 1.5 wavelengths, an observer hears:
questions.explain: A path difference of 1.5λ (an odd number of half-wavelengths) gives destructive interference, a minimum.

questions.q: White light passed through a diffraction grating produces spectra because:
options: Shorter wavelengths diffract more than longer ones
Longer wavelengths diffract more than shorter ones
All wavelengths diffract by the same angle
questions.explain: Since d sinθ = nλ, longer wavelengths (red) are diffracted through larger angles than shorter (violet).

questions.q: The refractive index of a medium is defined as:
options: The speed of light in the medium divided by speed in vacuum
The speed of light in vacuum divided by speed in the medium
questions.explain: Refractive index n = c/v, the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to its speed in the medium.

questions.q: In a double-slit experiment, slit separation is 0.50 mm, the screen is 2.0 m away and the fringe spacing is 2.4 mm. What is the wavelength of the light?
For a pipe closed at one end, the fundamental frequency forms a stationary wave with:
options: A node at the open end and antinode at the closed end
An antinode at the open end and node at the closed end
questions.explain: At a closed end air cannot move so a node forms; at an open end an antinode forms.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes transverse and longitudinal waves?
options: Both have oscillations perpendicular to energy transfer
In transverse waves oscillations are parallel to energy transfer
In longitudinal waves oscillations are perpendicular to energy transfer
In transverse waves oscillations are perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer
questions.explain: Transverse waves oscillate perpendicular to the direction of energy travel, longitudinal waves oscillate parallel to it.

questions.q: Two waves are described as coherent. This means they have:
options: A constant phase difference and the same frequency
questions.explain: Coherent sources maintain a constant phase difference and have the same frequency.

questions.q: For a stationary wave, which statement is true?
options: The wave profile moves at the wave speed
Adjacent points are always out of phase
All points between adjacent nodes oscillate in phase
Energy is transferred along the wave
questions.explain: Between two adjacent nodes all points oscillate in phase; no net energy is transferred along a stationary wave.

questions.q: A projectile is launched and lands at the same height. At the highest point of its path, its vertical velocity is:
questions.explain: At the peak the vertical component of velocity is momentarily zero.
